title: Spectral one-norm bounded by decision tree size
statement:
Let $T$ be a decision tree on $n$ Boolean variables, and let $g : \{0,1\}^n \to \{-1,1\}$ be the sign-encoded function it computes, sending an input $x$ to $\sigma(T(x))$ (with $\mathrm{false}\mapsto 1$ and $\mathrm{true}\mapsto -1$). Then the sum of the absolute values of its Fourier--Walsh coefficients is bounded by the size of $T$, i.e. its number of leaves:
\[
  \sum_{S \subseteq [n]} \bigl|\hat g(S)\bigr| \;\le\; \mathrm{size}(T),
\]
where the sum ranges over all subsets $S$ of $\{1,\dots,n\}$.
